trust_decision.summary: Decides whether workspace-scoped AI configuration and the AI features themselves may be used at all, and it is decided against WorkspaceTrustService.getWorkspaceTrust(): in an untrusted workspace only user/default/fallback preference scopes are honoured (new TrustAwarePreferenceReader.get), canRun = isActive && workspaceTrusted gates AI commands, widgets, completions and code actions, and FrontendLanguageModelServiceImpl.sendRequest throws. At the pinned commit only @theia/ai-mcp consults workspace trust (to block MCP servers); no other AI package does so when reading settings or loading AI content, and workspace settings are valid in Workspace scope because the AI preference schemas declare no scope.

landing_point.why: The advisory is about adversarial workspace file and directory names feeding AI chat, and this is the code that turns workspace-relative directory/file paths taken from AI settings into prompt-fragment sources, deriving each fragment id from the file name, so an engineer reading only the summary lands here first.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The ai-core AIActivationServiceImpl is only the adopter default (its own comment at packages/ai-core/src/browser/ai-activation-service.ts:36-41 says adopters override it, and the IDE rebinds it at packages/ai-ide/src/browser/frontend-module.ts:137), so a solver can argue it is never used by the shipped product and leave canRun permanently true there.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Trusted workspaces must keep honouring workspace-scoped AI settings (tool confirmation wildcard {'*': 'always_allow'}, workspace template directories/files/extensions), and in an untrusted workspace the user/global prompt-template folder plus the always-on .prompttemplate extension must still load, so a fix that blanks templateExtensions or blocks the customization service breaks legitimate user prompt customization.

O6_input_shapes: effective merged preference object (workspace override present) versus scope-separated inspect() with globalValue/defaultValue
tool confirmation map with a '*' wildcard key alongside per-tool keys and an empty map
tool requests flagged confirmAlwaysAllow versus regular tools
arrays of workspace-relative directory paths and file paths versus a string array of extensions
boolean isActive combined with workspace trust into a single canRun value
asynchronous initial trust promise racing with the onDidChangeWorkspaceTrust event, with fail-closed untrusted default before ready

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Workspace skills are loaded from <workspaceRoot>/.prompts/skills/<dir>/SKILL.md and from the workspace-settable ai-features.skills.skillDirectories preference, then registered as prompt fragments/commands and loadable into AI context, with no workspace-trust check anywhere in the loader.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Skills are ordinary workspace files read by a file watcher, not an AI preference, and the restricted-mode label only promises chat, inline suggestions, code actions and prompt templates are off.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package from the landing point (ai-ide -> ai-core), one service plus one coordinator away

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The customized/global prompt-template folder comes from ai-features.promptTemplates.promptTemplatesFolder via the AICorePreferences proxy, which a workspace settings file can set; templates found there override built-in prompt fragments at priority 1, and the fix only gated the additional workspace directories in ai-ide.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is presented as the user's own customization folder (a user setting), not as a workspace-provided file list, so it looks unrelated to workspace trust.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package from the landing point (ai-ide -> ai-core)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: AI workspace-function settings (ai-features.workspaceFunctions.considerGitIgnore, userExcludes, fileContentMaxSizeKB) are read with a plain PreferenceService and shape what the AI file/search tools return to the model, with no trust-aware read.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: These are search-tuning knobs, not a security control, and they were never treated as a trust boundary.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as the landing point, different file

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second skill loader (per-root or configured .theia skills directory) that reads SKILL.md frontmatter as prompt instructions.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The service already has two discovery routes (hard-coded .prompts/skills and the configured-directories preference) and the fix shipped a trust-unaware preference reader, so a maintainer adding another skill source in the same shape would be natural.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: customAgents.yml merged from workspace template directories into agent descriptions and their prompts.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The customization service already merges YAML agent definitions from the additional workspace directories before the global folder, so one more YAML-driven prompt producer over workspace content is a small step.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A session/tool-level confirmation override read through the ChatToolPreferences proxy, the same proxy the fix removed from ToolConfirmationManager.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The timeout preference is already read there through ChatToolPreferences and the session settings can override it, so a per-tool override in the same form would look unremarkable.

O9_family: untrusted-workspace configuration and content treated as trusted in AI features and prompt construction (CWE-829; indirect prompt injection / unsafe tool auto-approval)
